verdict.headline: Structural lean BULLISH (score +2.53), but the RELEASE itself is a weak same-day catalyst (conditional R²=0.00). Base case: the market is positioned for ~-3.8 MMbbl — the day's move hinges on the surprise vs that, and in this regime inventories are rarely the decisive driver.
factors: U.S. crude stocks are 1.3σ below the 5-year seasonal norm — structurally tight (bullish).
Last 4 weeks averaged a 6.7 MMbbl/week draw — bullish momentum into the print.
Cushing has drawn 5.8 MMbbl over 4 weeks (20.0 MMbbl now) — draining toward tank lows, very bullish for WTI structure.
Seasonally this week normally draws ~5.1 MMbbl (driving season); the model's expected change is -3.8 MMbbl.
Product alignment is 'mixed' — crude and products diverge, so the day-of read is muddier.

Release-day catalyst strength is a weak one: in the current High-vol / Backwardation / driving regime, the crude surprise has historically explained only R²=0.00 of the day's WTI move (n=30) — other drivers (macro, OPEC, positioning) usually dominate the day.

Asymmetry: a sizeable DRAW (~-3.8 MMbbl) is the base case and largely priced, so the bigger surprise risk is a BUILD (bearish). A draw merely in line confirms but adds little; a draw far bigger than -3.8 is the bullish tail.

verdict.headline: Neutral — model expects WTI to trade higher on the print (~0.20% on the surprise alone), confidence low.
factors: Surprise = -4.5 MMbbl (-0.8σ) vs expected — a larger draw / smaller build than priced in (bullish).
In the current High-vol / Backwardation regime, release-day WTI moves about 0.04% per 1 MMbbl of surprise (conditional R² 0.00, n=30) — inventories are a weak driver here.
Product alignment: mixed  — crude and products diverge, so the read is muddier.
